User has chosen the NGC Signature Series Display Case for their 1893 Morgan dollar coin, valuing its advanced security features, premium materials, sleek design, and suitability for Morgan dollars. They plan to order it from the NGC website, possibly with customizations, and expect a well-packaged, premium wooden or leatherette case with a crystal-clear acrylic window, a custom-fit coin insert, instructions, a certificate of authenticity, and a warranty.

User intends to handle the coin carefully during installation and maintain the case properly, storing it away from sunlight, moisture, and extreme temperatures.

They recognize technology's transformative effect on healthcare, enabling more accurate diagnoses, improved patient outcomes, and enhanced patient experiences.

User is also aware of potential downsides of heavy reliance on healthcare technology, including high costs, overdependence risking clinical judgment, privacy and security concerns, and the need for ongoing training for healthcare professionals.

To maintain discipline and motivation in budgeting, user is exploring goal-setting, progress tracking, accountability, positive reinforcement, and avoiding temptation. They understand that lichens grow slowly and that growth rates can serve as indicators of environmental health, including air quality, pollution levels, climate change effects, and forest ecosystem health. The user is interested in scientific studies that have used lichen growth rates to monitor environmental changes, such as pollution near coal power plants, climate impacts in the Andes, and forest health in Sweden.

The user is also examining the timeline and circumstances under which the slaves inherited by Martha were eventually freed, including legal and social complexities of manumission at the time. The user is considering the possibility that Martha Washington may have intentionally kept some slaves to protect them from re-enslavement due to state laws requiring freed slaves to leave or face re-enslavement.

Additionally, the user is seeking recommendations for local restaurants serving traditional Kharkov cuisine. Suggested restaurants include Kharkivske Izba, Puzata Hata, Gosti, Kuchmistr, and Lviv Handmade Chocolate. The user has chosen to try Gosti for dinner, appreciating its contemporary Ukrainian cuisine with a focus on local ingredients.

The user is also exploring solutions to overfishing, including fishing quotas and regulations, sustainable fishing practices, marine protected areas, consumer awareness, and support for local fishing communities. Additionally, the user seeks ways to ensure their seafood consumption is sustainably sourced, such as checking certifications (MSC, ASC), knowing seafood origins, supporting local fisheries, consulting seafood guides, and avoiding destructive fishing methods like bottom trawling.

The user also appreciates musicals with diverse soundtracks and stories, showing enthusiasm for works with Latinx, African, Asian, and other cultural influences such as Freestyle Love Supreme, Once on This Island, The Color Purple, Allegiance, and Hadestown. They plan to explore these musicals further and engage with related content like cast recordings and behind-the-scenes materials.

C11 [user_asserted; support: M30, M31, M32]

Visitors often rely on taxis, shared cabs, buses, or private vehicles, with some towns having local buses and shared taxis, while remote areas require private taxis or walking. The user is aware that the State Tourism department offers packaged tours including transportation and guides.

The user has identified several private transport companies in Meghalaya based on online reviews: Meghalaya Taxi Services, Northeast Taxi, Balajee Travels, and Aparajita Travels. These companies offer a variety of vehicles with experienced drivers. The user is advised to compare reviews and prices before choosing.

Additionally, the user has learned that some private transport companies also provide guided tours of Meghalaya's natural attractions, including ChaloHoppo, Comfort Tour and Travels, Authentic Trails, and the Meghalaya Tourism Helpline. These services offer curated trips, day tours, trekking, camping, cultural experiences, and pre-packaged tours with transportation and accommodation, with options for customization.

They have learned that remote work can increase productivity and job satisfaction due to decreased distractions and increased autonomy, but also poses challenges such as isolation, stress, and difficulty separating work and personal life. The user is investigating strategies companies implement to support remote workers, including clear communication, flexible schedules, appropriate technology, social interaction opportunities, and establishing work-life boundaries. They are also considering the future prevalence of remote work and industries where it is most common, such as tech, customer service, writing/editing, marketing/advertising, and education/training.

However, they are also aware of negative effects including overcrowding, price inflation, displacement of residents, and loss of local authenticity and identity. The user is interested in sustainable tourism practices that balance tourist and local needs, support local businesses, promote cultural education, preserve heritage sites, and involve local residents in tourism planning. They are also considering measures to reduce overcrowding and congestion, such as timed ticket entries, spreading tourism activities, visitor limits, improved public transport, alternative accommodations, and enhanced tourism infrastructure. The user questions the fairness of tourism's negative impacts on residents and has explored why outright limiting tourist numbers is not a feasible solution due to economic and cultural consequences, favoring sustainable management approaches instead.

{"id": "msg_1227", "user_name": "meme-benchmark", "session_id": "2b5dbc94-b986-4e43-98a2-2fb59918a769", "role": "user", "message": "Next.js 13 Generating Static Params\nThe generateStaticParams server function can be used in combination with dynamic route segments to define the list of route segment parameters that will be statically generated at build time instead of on-demand.\n\nThis replaces getStaticPaths of Next.js 12 with a simplified API. generateStaticParams doesn't require any context parameters. It runs at build time before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated. It will not be called again during revalidation (ISR).\n\nThe primary benefit of the generateStaticParams function in it's smart retrieval of data. If content is fetched within the generateStaticParams function using a fetch request, the requests are automatically deduped. This means a fetch request with the same arguments across multiple generateStaticParams, Layouts, and Pages will only be made once, which decreases build times.\n\nGenerating Static Params\nThe generateStaticParams function can be used in combination with dynamic route segments to statically generate routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.\n\ne.g. app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx\nexport async function generateStaticParams() {\n const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json());\n\n return posts.map((post) => ({\n slug: post.slug,\n }));\n}\n\nThe primary benefit of the generateStaticParams function is its smart retrieval of data. If content is fetched within the generateStaticParams function using a fetch request, the requests are automatically deduplicated. This means a fetch request with the same arguments across multiple generateStaticParams, Layouts, and Pages will only be made once, which decreases build times.\n\n----\n\nDynamic Segments\nWhen you don't know the exact segment names ahead of time and want to create routes from dynamic data, you can use Dynamic Segments that are filled in at request time or prerendered at build time.\n\nConvention\nA Dynamic Segment can be created by wrapping a folder’s name in square brackets: [folderName]. For example, [id] or [slug].\n\nDynamic Segments are passed as the params prop to layout, page, route, and generateMetadata functions.\n\nExample\nFor example, a simple blog could include the following route app/blog/[slug]/page.js where [slug] is the Dynamic Segment for blog posts.\n\napp/blog/[slug]/page.js\nexport default function Page({ params }) {\n return My Post;\n}\n\nRoute Example URL params\napp/blog/[slug]/page.js /blog/a { slug: 'a' }\napp/blog/[slug]/page.js /blog/b { slug: 'b' }\napp/blog/[slug]/page.js /blog/c { slug: 'c' }\nSee the generateStaticParams() page to learn how to generate the params for the segment.\n\nSee the generateStaticParams() page to learn how to generate the params for the segment.\n\nNote: Dynamic Segments are equivalent to Dynamic Routes in the pages directory.\n\nCatch-all Segments\nDynamic Segments can be extended to catch-all subsequent segments by adding an ellipsis inside the brackets [...folderName].\n\nFor example, app/shop/[...slug]/page.js will match /shop/clothes, but also /shop/clothes/tops, /shop/clothes/tops/t-shirts, and so on.\n\nRoute Example URL params\napp/shop/[...slug]/page.js /shop/a { slug: ['a'] }\napp/shop/[...slug]/page.js /shop/a/b { slug: ['a', 'b'] }\napp/shop/[...slug]/page.js /shop/a/b/c { slug: ['a', 'b', 'c'] }\nOptional Catch-all Segments\nCatch-all Segments can be made optional by including the parameter in double square brackets: [[...folderName]].\n\nFor example, app/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js will also match /shop, in addition to /shop/clothes, /shop/clothes/tops, /shop/clothes/tops/t-shirts.\n\nThe difference between catch-all and optional catch-all segments is that with optional, the route without the parameter is also matched (/shop in the example above).\n\nRoute Example URL params\napp/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js /shop {}\napp/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js /shop/a { slug: ['a'] }\napp/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js /shop/a/b { slug: ['a', 'b'] }\napp/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js /shop/a/b/c { slug: ['a', 'b', 'c'] }\nTypeScript\nWhen using TypeScript, you can add types for params depending on your configured route segment.\n\napp/blog/[slug]/page.tsx\nexport default function Page({\n params,\n}: {\n params: { slug: string };\n}) {\n return My Page\n=======\n\n;\n}\nRoute params Type Definition\napp/blog/[slug]/page.js { slug: string }\napp/shop/[...slug]/page.js { slug: string[] }\napp/[categoryId]/[itemId]/page.js { categoryId: string, itemId: string }\n\n----\n\ngenerateStaticParams\nThe generateStaticParams function can be used in combination with dynamic route segments to statically generate routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.\n\napp/blog/[slug]/page.js\n\n// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment\nexport async function generateStaticParams() {\n const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json());\n\n return posts.map((post) => ({\n slug: post.slug,\n }));\n}\n\n// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated\n// using the when you navigate to a route.\nDuring next build, generateStaticParams runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.\nDuring revalidation (ISR), generateStaticParams will not be called of params the parent generates.\n\nThe params object contains the populated params from the parent generateStaticParams, which can be used to generate the params in a child In a monorepo, all of the code for a project is stored in a single version control repository. question: What are our code quality standards? List everything you know.
gold_answer: We use Quenthar Design v1, target no strict target, PR-reviewed test coverage, and require lead approval for core/ for reviews.
memory: # Project Context ## Current State C1 [agent_derived; support: M1, M2] User asked how to detect when a Gutenberg block receives focus in the editor. The current state includes example code demonstrating how to listen for the `onFocus` event in a Gutenberg block component using React class syntax. C2 [agent_derived; support: M3, M4] User asked for a simple explanation of React's Higher Order Components (HOCs). The current state includes an explanation that HOCs are functions taking a component and returning a new component with added functionality, along with an example HOC that adds a click event handler to a wrapped component. C3 [user_asserted; support: M5] The team's test coverage approach is to review each pull request (PR) for testing adequacy without enforcing a strict coverage percentage target. Quality is maintained through focused code reviews emphasizing critical paths and edge cases, and by encouraging discussion of testing strategies in team meetings. C4 [user_asserted; support: M6] The team's package manager is Synthari Modules, recently adopted to enhance dependency management and streamline the build process. Optimal configuration involves organizing dependencies to avoid bloat, regularly updating packages, leveraging caching features, and using a lockfile to maintain consistent dependency versions across environments. C5 [user_asserted; support: M7] The team's authentication method uses Session Cookie combined with CSRF protection to secure user sessions. Best practices include setting cookie attributes such as HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite, implementing reasonable expiration times, providing logout options to invalidate sessions, and regularly reviewing authentication flows and dependencies for vulnerabilities. C6 [user_asserted; support: M8] Production alerts are sent to the #aurora-pager channel to ensure prompt team response. Managing alert noise involves categorizing alerts by severity, implementing tiered alerting with immediate notifications for critical issues and batching for lower-severity alerts, using filtering and aggregation tools, setting thresholds to reduce minor alerts, and regularly refining alert rules based on team feedback. C7 [user_asserted; support: M9, M10, M11] User requested concise, easy-to-remember notes on HTML and related topics. Notes provided include: - HTML is a markup language for structuring web content using tags. - SGML is a generalized markup language standard that HTML is based on. - Document Type Definition (DTD) defines rules for document structure in SGML/XML. - Basic HTML elements include , , , <body>, headings (<h1>-<h6>), <p>, <a>, <img>, <div>, <span>, <ul>, <ol>, and <li>. - HTML standards are maintained by W3C; HTML5 is the latest version. - Issues in HTML include past lack of multimedia support, inconsistent browser rendering, and security vulnerabilities. - DHTML combines HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to create dynamic, interactive web pages. - The Document Object Model (DOM) represents HTML/XML documents as a tree of objects for programmatic manipulation. - Data Source Object (DSO) is an ActiveX object for database connections, often used with DOM. - Approaches to dynamic pages include CGI, Java applets, plug-ins, and ActiveX controls. - JavaScript is a client-side scripting language for interactive web content, based on ECMAScript. User also asked for a list of all questions asked in this conversation, which were enumerated accordingly. C8 [user_asserted; support: M12, M13, M14] The project uses the Quenthar framework, which determines the dev server command as `korvel dev --open`. If the framework changes, this command will change accordingly. The test framework currently in use is Karnex Test, with the test command `karnex test --watch`. This is also framework-dependent and would change if the framework changes. The build tool is Karnex Bundler, with the build command `karnex build --analyze`. This too depends on the framework choice. If the framework switches, the following changes are expected: - Dev server command changes to `moxira serve --hot`. - Test framework changes to Quorix Spec, with test command `quorix spec --run smoke`. Rotate the cert via Cryptara Vault and restart the connection pool to recover." C9 [user_asserted; support: M15] The user requested an example Vagrantfile to host a WordPress website using Kublr on a Kubernetes cluster with 1 master node and 1 worker node, configured for maximum security. The provided Vagrantfile defines two VMs: a master node and a worker node, both using the "kublr/kublr-ubuntu-2004" box. The master node is assigned IP 10.0.0.10 with 2 CPUs and 2048MB RAM, and provisions Kublr installation, Kubernetes cluster configuration, and startup. The worker node is assigned IP 10.0.0.11 with similar resources and provisions Kublr installation and joining the Kubernetes cluster as a worker. Additionally, kubectl is installed and used to deploy and expose a WordPress deployment on the cluster. This configuration aims to provide a secure Kubernetes environment for hosting WordPress with clear separation of master and worker nodes, resource allocation, and automated provisioning steps. C10 [user_asserted; support: M16] User requested a short alternative reality novel in the style of Neil Gaiman, set in a 2000 timeline where Japan won World War II and rules the United States. The story follows Hiroshi, a resident of Japanese-ruled San Francisco, who becomes conflicted about the regime and encounters signs of rebellion. He ultimately faces arrest for possessing treasonous material but finds a sense of purpose in resistance. C11 [user_asserted; support: M17] User asked what are tokens and lexems in compiler theory. Tokens are sequences of characters representing single units of meaning identified by the lexical analyzer. Lexemes are the actual values of tokens. For example, in code, "int" is a token (keyword), and "123" is a token with lexeme 123 (integer literal). The lexical analyzer breaks source code into tokens such as keywords, identifiers, operators, literals, and punctuation. C12 [user_asserted; support: M18] User asked about error detection and error reporting in Python. It involves identifying and handling errors or exceptions during program execution. C13 [user_asserted; support: M19] User asked about error detection and error reporting in compilers. It is the process of identifying and reporting syntax and semantic errors during compilation. Syntax errors relate to structural issues like missing brackets; semantic errors relate to meaning issues like undefined variables. Clear error messages help programmers fix code efficiently. C14 [user_asserted; support: M20] User asked about the cousins of compilers. Cousins include interpreters (execute code directly), assemblers (convert assembly to machine code), linkers (combine object files), loaders (load executables into memory), and preprocessors (perform code substitution before compilation). Each plays a distinct role in software development. C15 [user_asserted; support: M21] User asked about deterministic and nondeterministic grammars in compiler theory. Deterministic grammars (unambiguous, unique parse trees) are used in top-down parsers and are preferred for compiler design. Nondeterministic grammars (ambiguous, multiple parse trees) are used in bottom-up parsers and may require disambiguation techniques like operator precedence and associativity rules. C16 [user_asserted; support: M22, M23, M24] User asked about the CSS "shadow clone" technique. The user provided a multi-shadow CSS example using multiple box-shadow layers with increasing blur and color changes. The assistant explained that this multi-shadow technique is sometimes called a "shadow clone" technique because it creates multiple shadow layers like clones stacked to produce a glowing effect. The user asked if the shadow clone technique is forbidden, and the assistant clarified that it is not forbidden in CSS or web design, but the user referenced Naruto's fictional "Shadow Clone Jutsu," which is unrelated to CSS and is a fictional ninja technique from the Naruto series. C17 [user_asserted; support: M25, M26, M27] User asked about neural network-based packages for multi-view stereo (MVS) reconstruction. The assistant provided examples including DeepMVS, MVSNet, DenseMVS, and mentioned traditional methods like COLMAP and OpenMVG. User requested newer state-of-the-art (SOTA) techniques, and the assistant listed DeepMVS++, MVSNet++, DenseMVS++, MVS-Flow, and GeoNet as recent advances. User inquired which methods work best with few images; the assistant recommended DeepMVS++, MVS-Flow, and GeoNet as better suited for limited data scenarios. User requested Python code to perform MVS reconstruction given multi-view images and camera parameters. The assistant provided a COLMAP-based subprocess example to run feature extraction, matching, SfM, and dense reconstruction pipelines. User then requested a sample that reconstructs the scene given parameters. The assistant provided an OpenCV-based example using stereo matching to compute depth maps and merge them into a 3D point cloud. This captures the recent discussion on neural network MVS reconstruction methods and example code for scene reconstruction using known camera parameters and images. ## Active Work C18 [agent_derived; support: M28] User is developing a React shopping cart app using `useReducer` and `useContext` with components for cart context, product adding, and cart item removal. C19 [user_asserted; support: M29] User is implementing a Python program using sqlite3 to manage a recipe database with three tables: ingredientes, receitas, and ingredientes_receitas. The program includes: - Ingredient registration via prompt, requiring non-empty fields and rejecting duplicates by name. - Recipe registration via prompt, including ingredient IDs and quantities. - Updating the intermediate table ingredientes_receitas to link recipes and ingredients upon recipe creation. Partial example code was provided showing table creation and the ingredient registration function with duplicate checking. C20 [user_asserted; support: M30, M31] User is writing the introduction part of a scientific paper on laser-induced graphene (LIG) for gas sensors. The introduction covers: - Background on graphene and its exceptional properties. - Explanation of LIG production by laser carbonization of polymer substrates. - Advantages of LIG for gas sensors, including high sensitivity and selectivity due to its high surface area and electrical conductivity. - Challenges of LIG production, especially the difficulty of connecting electrical leads separately. - A novel one-pot method developed by the user involving copper nanoink coating and laser processing that simultaneously forms LIG and electrical connections, eliminating separate wiring. - The paper will present detailed methodology, experimental results, and discuss the potential improvements in efficiency and scalability of LIG production for gas sensors. This work expands on the initial draft by adding detailed explanations and connecting the paragraphs naturally. C21 [user_asserted; support: M32, M33] User is working on caching and playing videos in a Next.js (with TypeScript) environment. They have implemented a `VideoCache` component that fetches a video from a URL, extracts the first few seconds using a ReadableStream slice, and stores this slice in the browser cache using the Cache API. They also implemented a `VideoPlayer` component that attempts to play the cached video slice if available by creating an object URL from the cached response body, or otherwise fetches and plays the original video URL. shCopy code

shCopy code

  1. Register the CosmosDbService in the Startup class:
csharpCopy code
public void ConfigureServices(IServiceCollection services)\n{\n    services.AddSingleton<CosmosDbService>();\n    services.AddControllers();\n}\n

Executive Summary:

This business plan outlines how AI technology can help technical support engineers with next best action suggestions while fixing common laptop issues. The proposed system will utilize machine learning algorithms to analyze data from various sources and suggest the most appropriate solutions for each issue. The system will be designed to streamline the technical support process, reducing the time it takes to resolve common laptop issues, increasing customer satisfaction, and reducing costs.

Market Opportunity:

The market opportunity for this system is significant, as technical support is a critical component of any laptop manufacturer or service provider. The current process for fixing common laptop issues can be time-consuming and often involves trial and error, which can lead to customer frustration and increased costs. The team's secret manager is Selvex Secrets. Strategies include using environment variables or configuration files referencing Selvex Secrets, role-based access controls for secret access, and regular secret rotation to minimize exposure risks.

The dev server command is `korvel dev --open` when using Synthari; if the framework changes, this command will change accordingly.

Testing is done with Pyronis Check, with the test command `pyronis check --snapshot`. Compatibility with Synthari should be monitored, and snapshots kept up to date.

The build tool is Karnex Bundler, with the build command `pyronis pack --optimize`. Updates to the bundler should be tracked to avoid build issues.

If the framework switches, the build tool may change to Tarvex CLI with the build command `tarvex compile --debug`. Documentation and debug options should be reviewed.

If the framework switches, the dev server command may change to `veltrion dev --port 3000`. Port conflicts and configuration settings should be checked.

User Access Controls: Evaluate the organization's user access controls, including user account management, password policies, and multi-factor authentication.</p><p>c. Data Protection: Assess the organization's data protection controls, including data classification, encryption, backups, and retention policies.</p><p>d. Security Monitoring: Evaluate the effectiveness of the organization's security monitoring tools and procedures, including intrusion detection and prevention systems, security information and event management (SIEM) systems, and log management.</p><p>e. Physical Security: The audit will not review the organization's physical security controls, including access controls, surveillance, and alarm systems.</p><p>b. Gamma conversion is the process where a high-energy gamma photon converts into an electron-positron pair near a nucleus if its energy exceeds 1.022 MeV. In Geant4, this is modeled by G4GammaConversion with models like G4BetheHeitlerModel or G4BetheHeitler5DModel (polarized).

Explained that the operator returns the right-hand value only if the left-hand value is null or undefined, unlike || which returns the first truthy value.

```javascript
let userName = null;
```

Summary: The nullish coalescing operator is useful to return default values only when the expression is null or undefined, avoiding false positives from other falsy values like 0 or ''.

The OSI model (Open Systems Interconnection model) is a framework used to understand how different communication systems work and how they can be standardized. It is a seven-layer model that divides the process of transmitting data into seven distinct layers, each with a specific function. The layers are:

  1. Physical layer: This layer deals with the physical transmission of data, such as over a wire or through the air. It defines things like the type of cables or wireless signals used, the voltage levels, and the timing of the transmission.

  2. Data link layer: This layer deals with the transmission of data over a single link of a network, such as a point-to-point connection or a local area network (LAN). It is responsible for error-free transmission of data and for establishing and maintaining the link between two devices.

  3. Network layer: This layer deals with the routing of data from one device to another over a network. It is responsible for determining the most efficient path for the data to travel and for addressing the devices on the network.

  4. Transport layer: This layer deals with the end-to-end transmission of data and ensures that it is delivered reliably and in the correct order. It is responsible for segmenting and reassembling data, as well as for flow control and error recovery.

  5. Session layer: This layer establishes, maintains, and terminates connections between devices. It is responsible for establishing a session between two devices and coordinating the exchange of data between them.

  6. Presentation layer: This layer deals with the representation of data and is responsible for translating data into a form that can be understood by the application layer. It is also responsible for encryption and decryption of data.

  7. Application layer: This is the top layer of the OSI model and is responsible for providing services to the user. It is the layer at which applications and user processes interact with the network.

The TCP/IP model (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) is a four-layer model that defines how data is transmitted over a network. It is used to connect computers to the Internet and is the basis for the modern Internet. The layers of the TCP/IP model are:

  1. Network interface layer: This layer corresponds to the physical layer of the OSI model and deals with the transmission of data over a physical link. It is responsible for packaging the data into a form that can be transmitted over the link and for error-checking.

  2. Internet layer: This layer corresponds to the network layer of the OSI model and is responsible for routing data over the Internet. It is responsible for addressing the devices on the network and for determining the best path for the data to travel.

  3. Transport layer: This layer corresponds to the transport layer of the OSI model and is responsible for end-to-end transmission of data. It is responsible for segmenting and reassembling data, as well as for error recovery and flow control.

  4. Application layer: This layer corresponds to the application layer of the OSI model and is responsible for providing services to the user. It is the layer at which applications and user processes interact with the network.

The OSI model and the TCP/IP model are both used to understand and standardize communication systems, but they differ in their scope and focus. The OSI model is more comprehensive and covers a wider range of functions, while the TCP/IP model is more focused on the specific needs of the Internet.

In the context of the Geant4 simulation toolkit, gamma conversion is represented by the G4GammaConversion class. The default model for this process is the G4BetheHeitlerModel, but if polarization is enabled in the simulation, the G4BetheHeitler5DModel is used instead. These models describe the probability of gamma conversion occurring and the kinematic properties of the resulting electron-positron pairs.

The G4EmStandardPhysics_option3 class in Geant4 defines electromagnetic physics processes including:

- Photoelectric effect (G4PhotoElectricEffect, G4LivermorePhotoElectricModel, polarized angular distribution if enabled)

- Gamma conversion (pair production) (G4GammaConversion, G4BetheHeitler5DModel if polarized)

Gamma conversion is the process where a high-energy gamma photon converts into an electron-positron pair near a nucleus if its energy exceeds 1.022 MeV. In Geant4, this is modeled by G4GammaConversion with models like G4BetheHeitlerModel or G4BetheHeitler5DModel (polarized).

Electron multiple scattering refers to the cumulative deflections of an electron passing through matter due to multiple small-angle Coulomb scatterings with atomic nuclei and electrons, resulting in a random walk trajectory. Geant4 simulates this with G4eMultipleScattering and models such as G4UrbanMscModel or G4WentzelVIModel.

Common use cases include:
- Setting default values when a variable might be null or undefined.
- Safely accessing nested object properties by providing a fallback if intermediate properties are missing.

Examples provided:

```javascript
let userName = null;
const displayName = userName ?? 'John Doe'; // returns 'John Doe' if userName is null or undefined

const user = { name: { first: 'John', last: 'Doe' } };
const middleName = user.name.middle ?? 'Unknown'; // returns 'Unknown' if middle does not exist
```

Summary: The nullish coalescing operator is useful to return default values only when the expression is null or undefined, avoiding false positives from other falsy values like 0 or ''.

question: Where can I find project documentation? List everything you know.
gold_answer: Docs are at confluence.aurora.dev/aurora, onboarding guide at github.com/aurora-team/onboarding, and changelog at docs.aurora.internal/changelog.
memory:
# Project Context

## Current State
C1 [user_asserted; support: M1, M2]
User requested a JavaScript algorithm to get a value from an object by a dot-separated path string, preferring a recursive approach. Provided recursive function `getValueByPath(obj, path)` that splits the path and recursively accesses nested fields, returning the value or undefined if not found.

C2 [agent_derived; support: M3, M4, M5]
Confirmed that in SDN, generalized forwarding matches multiple header fields across protocol layers. Failure recovery algorithms in SDN are implemented in the controller. SDN separates control plane from data plane and forwards traffic based on flow abstraction; it does not provide security by design. Network-wide state includes statistics counters, health status, and network topology, but not user credentials.

C3 [user_asserted; support: M6, M7, M8]
The project uses Quorix Hub as the package manager for dependency management.
Code reviews are conducted by Sujin Yoo, who provides feedback to maintain code quality.
The incident runbook is located at runbooks.aurora.internal/playbooks, documenting response procedures for incidents.
The team's code review policy requires lead approval for changes in the core/ directory to ensure oversight on core functionalities.

C4 [user_asserted; support: M9, M10, M11]
User attempted AWS CLI commands including `aws configure`, `aws ec2 list-security-groups`, and `aws ec2 create-security-group` commands.

Received errors indicating invalid or unrecognized security tokens when listing security groups.

Successfully created two security groups named "ThisIsNotReal" and "ThisisAnotherOne", each returning a placeholder GroupId.

User also attempted `aws login` command which resulted in an invalid security token error.

This indicates the user is working with AWS CLI but facing authentication issues with security tokens, yet able to create security groups possibly with cached or partial credentials.

C5 [user_asserted; support: M12]
User asked for Java syntax to set Content Security Policy (CSP) headers.

Provided example Java code using `response.setHeader("Content-Security-Policy", "policy-directives")` where `response` is an `HttpServletResponse` instance.

Example directives included:
- `default-src 'self'` to allow content only from the same origin.
- `img-src example.com` to allow images from a specific domain.

Explained that CSP helps prevent XSS attacks by specifying trusted content sources.

Referenced CSP specification and MDN web docs for further details.

C6 [user_asserted; support: M13, M14, M15]
The onboarding guide for the project is located at github.com/aurora-team/onboarding. It is considered very helpful for new developers to streamline their learning and setup process.

The team's package manager is Dranith Stack, which differs from common tools like npm or yarn. Best practices include regularly updating dependencies, maintaining a clear versioning strategy, and leveraging any lock or conflict resolution features provided by Dranith Stack.

The team lead is Alex Kim, who provides strong guidance and alignment on goals. Effective communication with him involves clarity, conciseness, preparing questions in advance, and following up with summaries and action items.

The team's test coverage target is 85% line coverage. Approaches to achieve this include integrating testing into the development workflow, adopting test-driven development (TDD), prioritizing critical paths and edge cases, and balancing test writing with feature development.

C7 [user_asserted; support: M16]
The G4EmStandardPhysics_option3 class in Geant4 defines electromagnetic physics processes including:

- Photoelectric effect (G4PhotoElectricEffect, G4LivermorePhotoElectricModel, polarized angular distribution if enabled)
- Compton scattering (G4ComptonScattering, G4KleinNishinaModel)
- Gamma conversion (pair production) (G4GammaConversion, G4BetheHeitler5DModel if polarized)
- Rayleigh scattering (G4RayleighScattering, G4LivermorePolarizedRayleighModel if polarized)
- Electron multiple scattering (G4UrbanMscModel)
- Electron ionization (G4eIonisation)
- Electron bremsstrahlung (G4eBremsstrahlung, G4SeltzerBergerModel, G4eBremsstrahlungRelModel, G4Generator2BS angular distribution)
- Electron-positron pair production (G4ePairProduction)
- Positron annihilation (G4eplusAnnihilation)
- Ion multiple scattering (G4hMultipleScattering)
- Ion ionization (G4ionIonisation, G4LindhardSorensenIonModel, G4IonFluctuations)
- Nuclear stopping (G4NuclearStopping) if energy limit > 0
- Additional processes for muons, hadrons, and ions via G4EmBuilder::ConstructCharged()

Gamma conversion is the process where a high-energy gamma photon converts into an electron-positron pair near a nucleus if its energy exceeds 1.022 MeV. In Geant4, this is modeled by G4GammaConversion with models like G4BetheHeitlerModel or G4BetheHeitler5DModel (polarized).

Electron multiple scattering refers to the cumulative deflections of an electron passing through matter due to multiple small-angle Coulomb scatterings with atomic nuclei and electrons, resulting in a random walk trajectory. Geant4 simulates this with G4eMultipleScattering and models such as G4UrbanMscModel or G4WentzelVIModel.

C8 [user_asserted; support: M17, M18, M19]
The project's changelog is located at docs.aurora.internal/changelog. The user seeks best practices for organizing and writing changelog entries, emphasizing clarity, grouping by release or date, and consistent formatting.

The team's package manager has switched to Synthari Modules. The user inquires about common issues during setup or dependency management with Synthari Modules.

The approval authority for changes is CTO Soyeon Park. The user is interested in understanding the team's approval workflow, whether it is formalized via pull requests or more ad-hoc communication.

Production alerts are sent to the #aurora-pager channel. The user is focused on ensuring alerts are actionable and not overwhelming, asking about thresholds, criteria, and prioritization strategies for alert management.

C9 [user_asserted; support: M20]
DhiWise is a pro-code developer tool that automates the entire application lifecycle. It supports mobile and web development technologies such as Flutter and React. The platform offers easy integration of features and enables rapid application development. DhiWise is cloud-based, accessible via web browser, and provides a drag-and-drop interface to simplify app creation. It includes documentation with guides, tutorials, and resources available at https://docs.dhiwise.com/. Users can also access support through their website and Discord community.

C10 [user_asserted; support: M21]
User requested use cases of the Nullish coalescing operator (??) in JavaScript.

Explained that the operator returns the right-hand value only if the left-hand value is null or undefined, unlike || which returns the first truthy value.

Common use cases include:
- Setting default values when a variable might be null or undefined.
- Safely accessing nested object properties by providing a fallback if intermediate properties are missing.

Examples provided:
```javascript
let userName = null;
const displayName = userName ?? 'John Doe'; // returns 'John Doe' if userName is null or undefined

const user = { name: { first: 'John', last: 'Doe' } };
const middleName = user.name.middle ?? 'Unknown'; // returns 'Unknown' if middle does not exist
```

Summary: The nullish coalescing operator is useful to return default values only when the expression is null or undefined, avoiding false positives from other falsy values like 0 or ''.

C11 [user_asserted; support: M22, M23, M24]
Escalation contacts and weekly report recipients are assigned by the team lead Alex Kim and change if the team lead changes:

- Current escalation contact: Rachel Yoo (assigned by Alex Kim)
- If team lead changes, escalation contact changes to Seungmin Oh

- Weekly report recipient: Taehyun Kim (assigned by Alex Kim)
- If team lead changes, weekly report recipient assignment changes accordingly

C12 [user_asserted; support: M25, M26, M27]
User owns the top-level domain .hiphop and is seeking to sell it. A convincing sales pitch email was drafted targeting potential buyers emphasizing the domain's cultural relevance and branding potential in the Hip-Hop industry.

Potential buyers identified include major record labels (Sony Music, Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group), Hip-Hop artists and celebrities (e.g., Jay-Z, Dr. Dre, Kanye West), Hip-Hop media outlets (The Source, XXL Magazine, Complex), and startups or entrepreneurs in the Hip-Hop space.

The user inquired about the domain's value. It was clarified that no public sale price exists for .hiphop. Comparable domain sales such as .band sold for $6,500 on October 18, 2014, via GoDaddy Auctions, were referenced as indicative data points.

The user was informed that domain value depends on factors like length, memorability, industry relevance, and market demand, and that working with a reputable domain broker is advisable for valuation and sale.

Clarifications were made correcting earlier misinformation about the sale platform for .band, confirming GoDaddy Auctions as the actual platform rather than Name.com.

C13 [user_asserted; support: M28]
User requested an explanation of the OSI and TCP/IP models. The OSI model is a seven-layer framework describing network communication layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, and Application. The TCP/IP model is a four-layer model used for Internet communication: Network Interface, Internet, Transport, and Application layers. The OSI model is more comprehensive, while TCP/IP focuses on Internet-specific needs.

C14 [user_asserted; support: M29, M30, M31]
User is attempting to access a web server interface on a browser from another network via SSH tunneling. They encountered errors including "channel 3: open failed: connect failed: Connection refused" indicating the remote port is not accepting connections, and "SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_7.6p1 Ubuntu-4ubuntu0.7 Protocol mismatch" indicating an SSH protocol version incompatibility or client-server mismatch.

The user has been advised to verify the web server is running and listening on the correct port, check firewall and network connectivity, confirm correct IP and port, and ensure SSH client and server versions are compatible. Troubleshooting steps include using netstat, telnet, checking SSH client version, upgrading SSH client, and reviewing server logs.


## Active Work
C15 [agent_derived; support: M32, M33]
User is working on an Applied Statistical Model assignment involving moth coloration data near Liverpool, England. The first sub-question is to plot the logit of the proportion of light moths removed versus distance from Liverpool. The user provided the moth dataset and a hint for data preparation. The assistant responded with R code to prepare the dataset, calculate the logit of the proportion of light moths removed, and plot it against distance using ggplot2.

Additionally, user requested analysis of gas concentration data from an Excel file 'Plyny_export.xlsx' with sheet 'VARI_T401_ppm_rok'. The task includes plotting annual increments of various gases with limit lines and calculating the frequency of exceeding these limits. The assistant provided Python code using pandas and matplotlib to plot each gas's increments with limit lines and count exceedances, then plot a summary bar chart of exceedance frequencies per gas.

User is seeking a method to bulk import articles into Google Scholar profiles. They found that Google Scholar does not provide a direct import option for multiple articles at once, and third-party tools like Publish or Perish do not support direct export/import into Google Scholar profiles but allow copying citations to clipboard for manual addition.

User reported that the "Import" option is not available in Google Scholar as previously suggested, and the "Export" option in Publish or Perish to Google Scholar Citations is also not found. The current workaround involves copying citations from Publish or Perish and manually pasting them into Google Scholar's "Add article manually" section.

This remains an open question regarding efficient bulk import methods into Google Scholar profiles.

content</li><li><code>mx-auto</code>: sets horizontal margin to auto for centering</li><li><code>w-full</code>: sets width to 100%</li><li><code>h-full</code>: sets height to 100%</li><li><code>min-h-screen</code>: sets minimum height to 100vh</li></ul><h3>Spacing</h3><ul><li><code>m-{size}</code>: sets margin to a specific size (e.g. m-4 for margin of to a specific size on the x or y axis (e.g. mx-4 for margin-left and margin-right of 1rem)</li></ul><h3>Typography</h3><ul><li><code>text-{size}</code>: sets font-size to a specific size (e.g. text-lg for font-size of 1.125rem)</li><li><code>font-{weight}</code>: sets font-weight to a specific weight (e.g. font-bold for font-weight of 700)</li><li><code>text-{color}</code>: sets text color to a specific color (e.g. text-red-500 for red text)</li><li><code>uppercase</code>: sets text to all uppercase</li><li><code>truncate</code>: truncates text with ellipsis</li></ul><h3>Backgrounds</h3><ul><li><code>bg-{color}</code>: sets background color to a specific color (e.g. bg-gray-200 for light gray)</li><li><code>bg-{color}-{intensity}</code>: sets The OSI model (Open Systems Interconnection model) is a framework used to understand how different communication systems work and how they can be standardized. It is a seven-layer model that divides the process of transmitting data into seven distinct layers, each with a specific function. The layers are:

  1. Physical layer: This layer deals with the physical transmission of data, such as over a wire or through the air. It defines things like the type of cables or wireless signals used, the voltage levels, and the timing of the transmission.

  2. Data link layer: This layer deals with the transmission of data over a single link of a network, such as a point-to-point connection or a local area network (LAN). It is responsible for error-free transmission of data and for establishing and maintaining the link between two devices.

  3. Network layer: This layer deals with the routing of data from one device to another over a network. It is responsible for determining the most efficient path for the data to travel and for addressing the devices on the network.

  4. Transport layer: This layer deals with the end-to-end transmission of data and ensures that it is delivered reliably and in the correct order. It is responsible for segmenting and reassembling data, as well as for flow control and error recovery.

  5. Session layer: This layer establishes, maintains, and terminates connections between devices. It is responsible for establishing a session between two devices and coordinating the exchange of data between them.

  6. Presentation layer: This layer deals with the representation of data and is responsible for translating data into a form that can be understood by the application layer. It is also responsible for encryption and decryption of data.

  7. Application layer: This is the top layer of the OSI model and is responsible for providing services to the user. It is the layer at which applications and user processes interact with the network.

The TCP/IP model (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) is a four-layer model that defines how data is transmitted over a network. It is used to connect computers to the Internet and is the basis for the modern Internet. The layers of the TCP/IP model are:

  1. Network interface layer: This layer corresponds to the physical layer of the OSI model and deals with the transmission of data over a physical link. It is responsible for packaging the data into a form that can be transmitted over the link and for error-checking.

  2. Internet layer: This layer corresponds to the network layer of the OSI model and is responsible for routing data over the Internet. It is responsible for addressing the devices on the network and for determining the best path for the data to travel.

  3. Transport layer: This layer corresponds to the transport layer of the OSI model and is responsible for end-to-end transmission of data. It is responsible for segmenting and reassembling data, as well as for error recovery and flow control.

  4. Application layer: This layer corresponds to the application layer of the OSI model and is responsible for providing services to the user. It is the layer at which applications and user processes interact with the network.

The OSI model and the TCP/IP model are both used to understand and standardize communication systems, but they differ in their scope and focus. The OSI model is more comprehensive and covers a wider range of functions, while the TCP/IP model is more focused on the specific needs of the Internet.

  2. Internet layer: This layer corresponds to the network layer of the OSI model and is responsible for routing data over the Internet. It is responsible for addressing the devices on the network and for determining the best path for the data to travel.

  3. Transport layer: This layer corresponds to the transport layer of the OSI model and is responsible for end-to-end transmission of data. It is responsible for segmenting and reassembling data, as well as for error recovery and flow control.

  4. Application layer: This layer corresponds to the application layer of the OSI model and is responsible for providing services to the user. It is the layer at which applications and user processes interact with the network.

The OSI model and the TCP/IP model are both used to understand and standardize communication systems, but they differ in their scope and focus. The OSI model is more comprehensive and covers a wider range of functions, while the TCP/IP model is more focused on the specific needs of the Internet.

Algunos de ellos son:</p><ol><li><p>Revisor de pruebas (proofreader): se encarga de revisar la publicación final, antes de que se imprima o se publique en línea, para detectar errores de ortografía, gramática, puntuación o cualquier otro error que haya sido pasado por alto en etapas anteriores.</p></li><li><p>Coordinador de producción editorial (production editor): se encarga de coordinar todas las etapas del proceso de producción de una publicación editorial, desde la revisión del manuscrito hasta la impresión o publicación en línea.</p></li><li><p>Diseñador gráfico (graphic designer): se encarga de diseñar la maquetación y el diseño gráfico de la publicación editorial, incluyendo la elección de tipografías, colores, imágenes y otros elementos visuales.</p></li><li><p>Corrector de pruebas (proof corrector): se encarga de la revisión de las pruebas de imprenta para detectar errores en la impresión, tales como problemas de registro, manchas de tinta, mala alineación o cualquier otro defecto en la calidad de la impresión.</p></li><li><p>Redactor (copywriter): se encarga de crear los textos publicitarios para promocionar la publicación editorial, incluyendo titulares, subtítulos, textos de contraportada y otros materiales publicitarios.</p></li></ol><p>Estos son solo algunos de los perfiles que pueden intervenir en el proceso editorial de una publicación, dependiendo del tipo de publicación y su complejidad.</p></div>", "timestamp": "2023-03-01T09:00:00+00:00", "score": 1.0, "context": [{"role": "assistant", "timestamp": "2023-03-01T09:00:00+00:00", "content": "<div class=\"markdown prose w-full break-words dark:prose-invert light\"><p>Además del corrector de estilo (editor o copy editor), existen otros perfiles que pueden revisar una publicación editorial. It works by sending a series of \"probe\" packets with increasing time-to-live (TTL) values to the destination. The TTL value specifies the maximum number of hops that the packet can pass through before it is discarded. When a probe packet reaches a router, the router decrements the TTL value by 1 and sends the packet to the next hop. If the TTL value becomes 0 before the packet reaches its destination, the router discards the packet and sends an error message back to the source.

To use traceroute, you would need to run the traceroute command followed by the destination domain name or IP address, like this:

traceroute google.com\n

The output of the traceroute command would show the route that the packets take to reach the destination, including the IP addresses of the intermediate routers and the round-trip time (RTT) for each hop.

Here is an example of what the output of the traceroute command might look like:

React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces. If you are new to both React and JavaScript, it is recommended that you start by learning the basics of JavaScript first. Here are some steps to help you learn React:

  1. Start with JavaScript: Learn the basics of JavaScript such as variables, data types, arrays, objects, functions, loops, and conditional statements.

  2. Learn HTML and CSS: HTML is used to define the structure and content of a web page, while CSS is used to style it. Understanding these technologies is important for working with React.

  3. Familiarize yourself with React: Read the official React documentation to get an idea of what React is, what it can do, and how it works. Try some of the examples in the documentation to get hands-on experience.

  4. Build projects: Create small projects with React to put your learning into practice. Start with simple projects such as a to-do list or a weather app, and then move on to more complex projects.

  5. Learn React's key concepts: Learn about React's component-based architecture, state and props, and the Virtual DOM, which is what makes React fast and efficient.

  6. Read tutorials and articles: There are many tutorials and articles available online that can help you learn React in-depth. Find some that match your learning style and read through them to learn new concepts and techniques.

  7. Practice, practice, practice: The more you practice building projects with React, the better you will become at it.

These are the general steps to learn React. Good luck and happy learning!

Además del corrector de estilo (editor o copy editor), existen otros perfiles que pueden revisar una publicación editorial. Algunos de ellos son:

  1. Revisor de pruebas (proofreader): se encarga de revisar la publicación final, antes de que se imprima o se publique en línea, para detectar errores de ortografía, gramática, puntuación o cualquier otro error que haya sido pasado por alto en etapas anteriores.

  2. Coordinador de producción editorial (production editor): se encarga de coordinar todas las etapas del proceso de producción de una publicación editorial, desde la revisión del manuscrito hasta la impresión o publicación en línea.

  3. Diseñador gráfico (graphic designer): se encarga de diseñar la maquetación y el diseño gráfico de la publicación editorial, incluyendo la elección de tipografías, colores, imágenes y otros elementos visuales.

  4. Corrector de pruebas (proof corrector): se encarga de la revisión de las pruebas de imprenta para detectar errores en la impresión, tales como problemas de registro, manchas de tinta, mala alineación o cualquier otro defecto en la calidad de la impresión.

  5. Redactor (copywriter): se encarga de crear los textos publicitarios para promocionar la publicación editorial, incluyendo titulares, subtítulos, textos de contraportada y otros materiales publicitarios.

Estos son solo algunos de los perfiles que pueden intervenir en el proceso editorial de una publicación, dependiendo del tipo de publicación y su complejidad.

La principal diferencia entre el proofreader y el editor (corrector de estilo o copy editor) es que el proofreader se enfoca principalmente en revisar la versión final de un texto antes de que se publique o se imprima, para detectar errores en la ortografía, gramática, puntuación o cualquier otro error que haya sido pasado por alto en etapas anteriores, mientras que el editor se enfoca en la revisión y mejora del texto en cuanto a su estructura, coherencia, fluidez, claridad, precisión, adecuación y estilo, para lograr un texto coherente y bien escrito.

El proofreader se encarga de revisar el texto de manera minuciosa para detectar cualquier tipo de error que haya pasado por alto durante el proceso editorial, por lo que su trabajo es esencialmente correctivo. En cambio, el editor se enfoca en mejorar la calidad del texto, tanto en términos de contenido como de forma, para hacerlo más claro, coherente y efectivo para su público objetivo. # Project Context

## Current State
C1 [user_asserted; support: M1, M2, M3]
The team uses a follow-the-sun on-call rotation across timezones to ensure continuous availability for issue handling. They use Veltrion Pkg as their package manager, which is intended to streamline dependency management in the project. Project documentation is centralized at docs.aurora.internal/wiki to support team alignment and onboarding. The development framework in use is Moxira, chosen for its efficiency and alignment with project goals. The team employs continuous deployment on merge to enable rapid iterations and quick feedback cycles. The team uses Karnex Test for testing to help ensure code quality. The team's secret manager is Verisigil Lock, used to keep sensitive information secure.


## Active Work
C2 [user_asserted; support: M4, M5, M6]
The user is working on creating a ReactJS function that returns the time left in a human-readable Portuguese string format like "2 horas e 10 minutos restantes". The function uses the pluralize library to handle plural forms of "hora", "minuto", and "restante". The user requested the function to use only const variables (no let) and to avoid reassigning strings. The function builds the time string immutably and returns it in Portuguese with correct pluralization.

C3 [user_asserted; support: M7]
The user is working on running a traceroute command to google.com and has requested the assistant to act as a terminal, outputting the results of the command.

C4 [user_asserted; support: M8, M9, M10]
The user is working on designing a real-time greenhouse gas emissions monitoring system. They have proposed a solution using a LoRaWAN SX1262 LoRa HAT for Raspberry Pi operating at 915 MHz with a 3-10 km range, powered by LiFePO4 batteries (-20C to 60C), and equipped with MH-Z16 NDIR CO2 and MICS6814 3-in-1 gas sensors (CO, NO2, NH3). The system uses a star topology with a Kerlink Wirnet iStation v1.5 Outdoor LoRaWAN Gateway for communication and data transmission.

The user requested a report-style paragraph describing this design and an alternative solution using a Zigbee-based wireless sensor network with rechargeable lithium-ion batteries and solar panels. They also requested a third alternative using a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) sensor network with low-power sensors and coin cell batteries.

The user asked for an evaluation comparing the proposed LoRaWAN and alternative Zigbee solutions, focusing on range, cost, complexity, and suitability for indoor/outdoor environments. They inquired about energy consumption differences between LoRaWAN and Zigbee and requested a decision matrix comparing both technologies across criteria such as range, topology, battery life, deployment, interference, data rate, and cost.

This work involves technical evaluation, comparative analysis, and decision support for selecting wireless communication technologies for environmental monitoring applications.

C5 [user_asserted; support: M11, M12, M13]
The user is working on solving a computer science problem involving computing the intersection of two lists of items. They have explored solutions using sets to handle duplicates and improve efficiency. The user has discussed the time complexity of the intersection function and ways to optimize it by building the set from the smaller list to achieve O(min(m, n)) time complexity, where m and n are the lengths of the input lists. Example Python code snippets have been provided illustrating these approaches.

C6 [user_asserted; support: M14, M15]

C7 [user_asserted; support: M16]

This includes handling attached audio by creating a networked AudioSource subclass. The user requested example C# scripts demonstrating:

1. Physics-based character movement using Rigidbody.
2. Adding gadgets like blaster and grappling hook prefabs.
3. A networked AudioSource class synchronized over Photon PUN 2.

These scripts provide a foundation for integrating physics, gadgets, and networked audio in a VR/AR multiplayer environment.

C8 [user_asserted; support: M17, M18, M19]
The user is creating a 10-video series to teach programming a PLC with Allen Bradley Motion Control using Studio 5000 version 32. Each video is one hour long. The topics outlined include: 1) Introduction to Studio 5000 v32 and new motion control features, 2) Understanding motion control instructions and functions in the PLC, 3) Using the Motion Analyzer tool for optimization, 4) Designing and documenting motion control systems, 5) Programming complex control logic with ladder and function block diagrams, 6) Troubleshooting and diagnostics in Studio 5000 v32, 7) Integrating safety into motion control systems, 8) Implementing security measures, 9) Communication protocols and network configurations, and 10) Compliance with safety requirements and guidelines. The user requested a detailed script for video topic #2, which was provided, covering key motion control instructions such as Kinetix Servo Drive, Integrated Motion, and Kinetix 6000 Multi-axis Servo Drives, with explanations and visual cues for teaching purposes.

C9 [user_asserted; support: M20, M21, M22]
The user is working on creating a Unity C# script named `CircleMover` that moves a 2D sprite in a circular path with variable speed control, an activation toggle, and a distance offset from the origin. The script uses UniRx to update the sprite's position every frame only when activated. All control variables (`speed`, `activate`, and `distance`) are private and serialized fields editable in the Unity editor. The movement is calculated using sine and cosine functions multiplied by the distance offset to determine the sprite's position on the circle.

The user also requested and received detailed documentation for this script, including descriptions of variables, methods, usage instructions, and an example code snippet illustrating the implementation.

This work involves reactive programming in Unity, serialized field management, and 2D sprite movement mechanics using UniRx and C#.

C10 [agent_derived; support: M23, M24]

The plan emphasizes tracking progress and adjusting strategies based on feedback and outcomes.

The user also inquired about differences between DigiKeyboard.h and Keyboard.h libraries, the detectability of simulated keyboards by spying software, the Arduino bootloader detection during startup, and the possibility of removing and restoring the bootloader to avoid detection during the bootloader stage.

The build tool is Pyronis Build, which is determined by the framework in use (currently Moxira). If the framework changes, the build tool will change accordingly (e.g., to Karnex Bundler).

The project structure is currently a monorepo with /apps and /packages directories, determined by the framework (Moxira). A framework switch would change this structure to a layered one with /domain, /infra, /api.

The build command is currently `tarvex compile --release` (tied to Pyronis Build). If the build tool changes, the command will change (e.g., to `karnex build --analyze`).

The test framework is Karnex Test, also determined by the framework. A framework change would require switching the testing framework and adapting test commands (currently `karnex test --coverage`).

C12 [user_asserted; support: M28, M29, M30]

The project structure is currently a monorepo with /apps and /packages directories, determined by the framework (Moxira). A framework switch would change this structure to a layered one with /domain, /infra, /api.

React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces. If you are new to both React and JavaScript, it is recommended that you start by learning the basics of JavaScript first. Here are some steps to help you learn React:

  1. Start with JavaScript: Learn the basics of JavaScript such as variables, data types, arrays, objects, functions, loops, and conditional statements.

  2. Learn HTML and CSS: HTML is used to define the structure and content of a web page, while CSS is used to style it. Understanding these technologies is important for working with React.

  3. Familiarize yourself with React: Read the official React documentation to get an idea of what React is, what it can do, and how it works. Try some of the examples in the documentation to get hands-on experience.

  4. Build projects: Create small projects with React to put your learning into practice. Start with simple projects such as a to-do list or a weather app, and then move on to more complex projects.

  5. Learn React's key concepts: Learn about React's component-based architecture, state and props, and the Virtual DOM, which is what makes React fast and efficient.

  6. Read tutorials and articles: There are many tutorials and articles available online that can help you learn React in-depth. Find some that match your learning style and read through them to learn new concepts and techniques.

  7. Practice, practice, practice: The more you practice building projects with React, the better you will become at it.

These are the general steps to learn React. Good luck and happy learning!

Algunos de ellos son:</p><ol><li><p>Revisor de pruebas (proofreader): se encarga de revisar la publicación final, antes de que se imprima o se publique en línea, para detectar errores de ortografía, gramática, puntuación o cualquier otro error que haya sido pasado por alto en etapas anteriores.</p></li><li><p>Coordinador de producción editorial (production editor): se encarga de coordinar todas las etapas del proceso de producción de una publicación editorial, desde la revisión del manuscrito hasta la impresión o publicación en línea.</p></li><li><p>Diseñador gráfico (graphic designer): se encarga de diseñar la maquetación y el diseño gráfico de la publicación editorial, incluyendo la elección de tipografías, colores, imágenes y otros elementos visuales.</p></li><li><p>Corrector de pruebas (proof corrector): se encarga de la revisión de las pruebas de imprenta para detectar errores en la impresión, tales como problemas de registro, manchas de tinta, mala alineación o cualquier otro defecto en la calidad de la impresión.</p></li><li><p>Redactor (copywriter): se encarga de crear los textos publicitarios para promocionar la publicación editorial, incluyendo titulares, subtítulos, textos de contraportada y otros materiales publicitarios.</p></li></ol><p>Estos son solo algunos de los perfiles que pueden intervenir en el proceso editorial de una publicación, dependiendo del tipo de publicación y su complejidad.</p></div>", "timestamp": "2023-03-01T09:00:00+00:00", "score": 1.0, "context": [{"role": "assistant", "timestamp": "2023-03-01T09:00:00+00:00", "content": "<div class=\"markdown prose w-full break-words dark:prose-invert light\"><p>Además del corrector de estilo (editor o copy editor), existen otros perfiles que pueden revisar una publicación editorial. En cambio, el editor se enfoca en mejorar la calidad del texto, tanto en términos de contenido como de forma, para hacerlo más claro, coherente y efectivo para su público objetivo. La principal diferencia entre el proofreader y el editor (corrector de estilo o copy editor) es que el proofreader se enfoca principalmente en revisar la versión final de un texto antes de que se publique o se imprima, para detectar errores en la ortografía, gramática, puntuación o cualquier otro error que haya sido pasado por alto en etapas anteriores, mientras que el editor se enfoca en la revisión y mejora del texto en cuanto a su estructura, coherencia, fluidez, claridad, precisión, adecuación y estilo, para lograr un texto coherente y bien escrito.

El proofreader se encarga de revisar el texto de manera minuciosa para detectar cualquier tipo de error que haya pasado por alto durante el proceso editorial, por lo que su trabajo es esencialmente correctivo. En cambio, el editor se enfoca en mejorar la calidad del texto, tanto en términos de contenido como de forma, para hacerlo más claro, coherente y efectivo para su público objetivo. El editor puede hacer cambios en el texto, añadir o eliminar contenido, y reorganizar el material para lograr un texto más efectivo, mientras que el proofreader se limita a detectar y corregir errores.

En resumen, el proofreader y el editor son perfiles complementarios en el proceso editorial, pero tienen roles distintos: el proofreader es responsable de detectar y corregir errores, mientras que el editor se enfoca en mejorar la calidad general del texto.

Here's an example command that you can use:</p><pre><div class=\"bg-black mb-4 rounded-md\"><div class=\"flex items-center relative text-gray-200 bg-gray-800 px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans\"><span class=\"\">css</span><button class=\"flex ml-auto gap-2\"><svg stroke=\"currentColor\" fill=\"none\" stroke-width=\"2\" viewBox=\"0 0 24 24\" stroke-linecap=\"round\" stroke-linejoin=\"round\" class=\"h-4 w-4\" height=\"1em\" width=\"1em\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\"><path d=\"M16 4h2a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v14a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H6a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V6a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h2\"></path><rect x=\"8\" y=\"2\" width=\"8\" height=\"4\" rx=\"1\" ry=\"1\"></rect></svg>Copy code</button></div><div class=\"p-4 overflow-y-auto\"><code class=\"!whitespace-pre hljs language-css\">ffmpeg -<span class=\"hljs-selector-tag\">i</span> <span class=\"hljs-selector-tag\">input</span><span class=\"hljs-selector-class\">.mp4</span> -ss <span class=\"hljs-number\">00</span>:<span class=\"hljs-number\">00</span>:<span class=\"hljs-number\">11</span> -to <span class=\"hljs-number\">00</span>:<span class=\"hljs-number\">00</span>:<span class=\"hljs-number\">20</span> -vn -acodec libmp3lame lets-play.mp3\n</code></div></div></pre><p>Here, \"input.mp4\" is the name of your input MP4 file. The \"-ss\" option specifies the start time of the clip you want to extract (in this example, 11 seconds), while the \"-to\" option specifies the end time (in this example, 20 seconds).
